clues.title: Solicitor appointment card in Elias's pocket
clues.description: Found in Elias's coat pocket: a card from Whittle & Cross confirming a 10:00 appointment 're: will amendment, final signature.' Elias had made arrangements to change his will this morning.

clues.title: 'Nadia will not be pleased'
clues.description: Elias's notebook, yesterday's entry: 'Called W&C — appointment confirmed. Nadia will not be pleased, but it is my estate and not the clinic's to decide.' He was removing the clinic from his will — and he knew Nadia would object.

clues.title: Original bequest — clinic as beneficiary
clues.description: In the clinic filing cabinet: a letter from Elias two years ago directing his cottage estate to the clinic fund on his death. Nadia's initials mark the file — she was involved in establishing this arrangement.

clues.title: Dispensary log — altered digoxin entry
clues.description: Monday's dispensary log shows a digoxin entry crossed out and rewritten in different ink — the surrounding entries are all in Nadia's usual blue biro; the correction uses black. The rewritten dosage is lower than what was originally recorded.

clues.title: Two unknown capsules in the pill organiser
clues.description: The pill organiser recovered from the bench: the Tuesday morning compartment contains two pale yellow capsules that are not Elias's prescribed tablets. His prescription is for white digoxin 0.125mg tablets. The pale capsules appear to be a higher-dose formulation.

clues.title: Nadia handed Elias the pills at 07:05
clues.description: Ruth saw Nadia cross the square at 07:05 and give Elias something small from her hand. Elias took it with his tea. Ruth thought nothing of it — it was Nadia's routine.

clues.title: Ruth saw Elias take the pills
clues.description: Ruth specifically recalls watching Elias swallow the pills — he tipped his head back and drank from his flask straight after. She thought it sweet that the nurse looked after him personally.

clues.title: Elias was healthy at 07:00
clues.description: Ruth passed Elias at 07:00 — he waved his flask at her in his usual greeting. He was perfectly alert. He died within twenty-one minutes of Nadia's visit.

clues.title: Elias's hand on his chest at 07:15
clues.description: Ben passed the bench at 07:15 and noticed Elias had one hand pressed to his chest. Elias's posture had changed — he was leaning rather than sitting upright. Ben assumed he was cold.

clues.title: Nadia's estate budget projections
clues.description: Hidden in a locked drawer in the clinic: Nadia's personal notebook. A page at the back is headed 'Estate update — Elias', followed by projected clinic renovations and equipment purchases — all funded by the expected bequest. The amounts run into six figures.

clues.title: Elias's prescription — correct dosage on file
clues.description: Dr. Haig's prescription file for Elias Grant: 0.125mg digoxin once daily. Two 0.25mg capsules would deliver four times his safe dose — fatal given his existing cardiac condition.

clues.title: Elias appeared to be asleep at 07:30
clues.description: Clara noticed from the cafe window at 07:30 that Elias looked oddly slumped on his bench. She assumed he'd dozed off — he often did on warm mornings. She did not go out to check.

clues.title: Ben's debt notice in Elias's coat
clues.description: A county court notice in Elias's coat: Ben Carter's father owed Elias £1,200. Ben had recently complained to Clara that he 'wished that old debt would just disappear'. On the surface a motive — in practice, trivial.

clues.title: Ben's round is corroborated
clues.description: Ben's delivery receipts, timestamped by three separate shopkeepers, place him at the square only briefly at 07:15 — too late to have tampered with the pills before Nadia delivered them.

conclusions.summary: Elias had directed his cottage estate to the clinic in his will — an arrangement Nadia managed and depended on. He was changing it this morning. Nadia's budget projections show how much she had invested in this bequest.
Nadia had access to and knowledge of digoxin, prepared Elias's pills unsupervised, and falsified the dispensary log to conceal the overdose.
Nadia was the last person to see Elias alive. She handed him the pill organiser at 07:05. He was healthy at 07:00 and dead by 07:21 — entirely within Nadia's window of contact.
Elias died of digoxin overdose at 07:21. The extra capsules in the pill organiser were not his prescription. His collapse followed Nadia's pill handoff by sixteen minutes.
Ben had a family debt to Elias and had expressed a wish it would 'go away'. A superficial motive.
Ben's timestamped delivery receipts account for his movements; he had no access to Elias's pills.
